checks.name: central_question_resolved
checks.evidence: Central question: 'Will Neela kill the husband she was sold to?' The answer is no. In ch 11 she holds the killing point for three breaths, then lifts her hand: 'Your guard drops on the left.' In ch 14 she kills the ambush scouts to keep him alive. In ch 25–27 she rides into the Resin House for his antidote and pours it into his mouth. In ch 30 she hands him the contract tooth and tells him the whole contract. The external plot also closes: Ittan, the buyer, is arrested under border law in ch 29, and the pass is sealed. The questions left open are the series hinge (the queen's seal, ch 32) and logged series threads.

checks.name: clues_paid_off
checks.evidence: All 20 clues with chapter payoffs pay off on the page. C01–C05 pay off in ch 16, when she rereads the shutters, kennelled hounds, 'the cat', unlit lamp and 'Not tonight, Janu'. C06 and C07 pay off in ch 27 ('That's all the verse ever was'). C08 and C09 pay off in ch 26, where Kirri is the civet wearing the silver anklet. C15, C17, C26 and C30 pay off in ch 29: the wax matches Asha's token, the slip is read aloud, the writ clause is read aloud, and Ittan's own climb to the pass leads to his arrest. C18 and C19 pay off in ch 32, where the green sunbird seal matches the gift seal and the queen is revealed as the hand behind Ittan. C24 and C25 pay off in ch 21 (the captain at twenty-four). C27 pays off in ch 30 (the tooth). C31 pays off in ch 31 (the pebble on the sill). C32 pays off in ch 30 (why he barred the shutters). The 12 'series' clues are all planted on the page and logged below. Minor note on C32: in ch 3 his answer about the shutters is 'Rain'. The literal 'I won't answer that' in ch 3 is given to 'Why did your council choose me?' The payoff still lands, but the outline wording does not match the text.

checks.name: midpoint_reversal
checks.evidence: In ch 16 (the midpoint) Devan withdraws the bargain he offered in ch 15: 'I withdraw it. The whole of it... What I saw, I keep... It's yours.' Asked why, he says: 'Because I don't want to own anyone.' Neela then rereads the whole first half as a fence he built to protect her, rather than a trap. This changes the romance. He gives up power over her with no terms. She sleeps human beside him for the first time as a test of trust, and the honest dark-talk terms of ch 17 follow from it.

checks.name: heroine_belief_change
checks.evidence: Opening belief (ch 7): 'If anyone ever saw me, Ammu, I'd be finished.' In ch 1 she guards every witness and fears a third would 'hold a cage in his mouth'. The proof is in ch 27, when she chooses to name her night-shape to the one person who is looking: 'She had never said it... To him, then. Her voice cracked and held. "Leopard."' In ch 1 she could not have chosen to make herself seen. Ch 30 confirms the new belief: 'There's rain on my neck and a man who's seen all of me, and I'm not counting the door.' Ch 31 adds a second choice: she turns back 'in his arms... the first time she has let anyone see the return.'

checks.name: real_loss
checks.evidence: Ammu dies in ch 27 drawing Vellan and the hunters away: 'jackal blood, hot and sharp, and nothing living under it.' She is buried in ch 28 and stays dead, named again in the daylight vows of ch 31. Raiu is mauled and dies under Neela's hands in ch 25. Kirri's caging is confirmed irreversible in ch 28: 'A cage could be unlocked. A caging could not.' Neela's guild page also burns, which makes her rogue for good.

checks.name: love_interest_goal
checks.evidence: Devan's goal is to find the councillor selling genuine-wax pass-tokens to Thurai raiders. In ch 4: 'Someone on the queen's council.' / 'If I knew, he'd be in a cell.' The goal is driven by Asha's death (ch 12, her first token) and Raman's widow and son (ch 7, ch 15). It predates the marriage and does not depend on Neela. It concludes with Ittan's arrest in ch 29.

checks.name: series_hinge
checks.evidence: In ch 32 the payment writ to the Resin House for the warden's death is sealed with the queen's own green sunbird wax. It matches the wedding-gift seal: 'She sealed the box with her own hand and the writ with her own hand.' This opens the bigger question: 'If the crown paid the guild, what else does the queen own?' The teaser ties to the next book: Neela will take Chathu's ledger and Devan will come, with Kirri still caged and Muthu's grey-wax packet waiting in the strongbox for the spring rider.

series_threads.thread: Neela's dread at the broken-beaked parrot newel and her compulsive counting on the west stair suggest a buried link between her and the stair where Asha died.
Asha always drew her parrot with a whole beak and called the broken newel 'an insult to a bird'. The beak breaking ties to C10 and the west stair.
Neela counts stair steps in her sleep and whimpers 'It's broken.' This suggests a lost or suppressed memory, possibly from before she was sold at six.
Raiu's bear claw marks on the west stair match Asha's wounds. Devan's realisation is cut off by the poison. Was Vellan Asha's killer, and who let him inside the walls?
The sloth bear (Vellan) guarding the Resin House. Vellan survives, lamed, and fled with Chathu.
Muthu's plain grey-wax letters 'to his mother'. Is he reporting to the palace? His grey packet is held unread for the spring rider.
Fresh Varanad mint silver carried by the raider scouts suggests the crown funds the raids. Raised again in ch 32.
Chathu: 'the ledger isn't the only book.' A second book or record, perhaps the queen's, which Neela now means to take.
Neela knows a goat path on the pass without a map, which hints at a childhood in the Kettamala hills.
Neela's unexplained gagging at crushed lantana, another lost-origin clue alongside C22 and C12.
Muthu goes quiet over the second letter. Someone leaked the cart order to Chathu. Muthu's loyalty is unresolved.
Vellan's carved bird left inside the barred chamber shows someone inside the fort let him in or told him where the sword lay. This ties to C28.

summary: The book meets all seven book-level checks. The central question is answered: Neela never kills Devan, and the turn runs from the pulled strike (ch 11) through the antidote ride and self-naming (ch 27) to the tooth confession (ch 30). Devan's outward goal, the token-seller, also closes with Ittan's arrest in ch 29. Every clue with a chapter payoff lands on the page, and the twelve series clues are all planted and logged as threads. The midpoint in ch 16, where Devan withdraws the bargain, recasts the first half and changes the romance. The heroine's belief change is shown by a choice, 'Leopard', spoken to him, not told. Ammu's and Raiu's deaths and Kirri's caging are real, permanent losses. Ch 32 opens a crown-level hinge with the queen's seal. One small fix for the owner: the outline says Devan refused the shutters question in ch 3 with 'I won't answer that', but on the page he says 'Rain'. His 'I won't answer that' in ch 3 goes to 'Why did your council choose me?' The ch 30 payoff still works, but the outline note or the ch 3 line should be aligned. Muthu's loyalty and the source of the inside leak are deliberately left open as series threads.
